numericalReview: 60*20=1200 IU;1200/150=8 mL;1200/300=4 mL. Dilution does not change dose. Label and final scenario review still pending. Independently calculated 20*22.5=450 mg amoxicillin/dose;450*2=900 mg/day;450<875 mg dose cap. No suspension volume asserted without a selected product. HyperRab example:4 mL*300 IU/mL=1200 IU;4 mL product+4 mL D5W=8 mL total;1200/8=150 IU/mL after dilution, unchanged total dose.
discrepancies: IDSA 2014 bite section summary uses 10-year tetanus language and evidence text uses greater-than thresholds; use current CDC inclusive 5-year dirty-wound and 10-year clean-wound thresholds.

NICE pediatric alternative co-trimoxazole differs from IDSA mixed-flora advice to add anaerobic cover when TMP-SMX is used; pediatric allergy regimen needs explicit current US pathway review before teaching a default.

RCH pediatric guidance recommends minimum 14-day treatment for infected wounds versus NICE five days for most bites; retain explicit source and severity context, with further US regimen review pending.

General CDC PEP page gives a broad no-HRIG prior-vaccination rule; Yellow Book immunocompromised subsection supplies material exceptions. Teach specialist assessment using that more specific guidance.

UCSF pediatric bite treatment is 7-10 days and adult pathway 10 days, versus NICE initial 5 days and RCH minimum 14 days; source-specific durations are identified and deep infection excluded from a universal course.

September 2026 CDC algorithm groups equids/livestock with domesticated animals above an observation branch; specific CDC veterinarian guidance defines the ten-day observation for dogs, cats and ferrets. Module limits the rule to those three and refers other species to public health.

FDA-hosted Imovax July 2025 and RabAvert inserts retain five-dose PEP for previously unvaccinated people. Current CDC guidance specifies four doses for unvaccinated immunocompetent patients. Module explicitly teaches CDC schedule and documents label difference.

Imovax label specifies five-dose PEP for immunosuppression irrespective of prior vaccination; Yellow Book provides a narrower documented-response/no-immune-change exception. Public-health review remains required rather than silently blending the sources.
